draft.title: Stalin's rise to power
card: Lenin died in January 1924. No single leader replaced him, and several senior Bolsheviks, including Trotsky, Zinoviev, Kamenev and Bukharin, competed for influence in the party.
Stalin was general secretary of the party. The post gave him control over party appointments, so he could place supporters in important jobs and local branches.
Those supporters later voted for him at party meetings and congresses. His power came from support inside the party machine, not from being the best-known or most admired figure.
Stalin defeated his rivals one at a time. He joined with some against others, then turned on his former partners. Trotsky was removed from the party and sent into exile in 1929.
draft.remember: Stalin won by controlling party positions and support, and by defeating his rivals one at a time.

a.q: How did Stalin's post as general secretary help him defeat his rivals?
opts: It let him place supporters in party positions
It gave him command of the Red Army
It made him Lenin's named successor
It let him ban rival members from all meetings
a.why: The post gave Stalin control over party appointments, so he built a base of supporters who backed him in party votes. The card does not say he commanded the army, and his rise did not depend on military force.
a.clue: Think about who got the jobs in the party.

b.q: Why was Trotsky, who was widely known and admired, unable to stop Stalin gaining power?
opts: Stalin held more support inside the party machine
Stalin was better known to the public than Trotsky
Trotsky had joined with Stalin against the other rivals
Trotsky had refused to take part in party meetings
b.why: Power in the party depended on support among its members and officials, and Stalin's control of appointments gave him more of it. Fame did not decide the contest. Being well known was Trotsky's strength, so the option saying Stalin was better known is wrong.
b.clue: Who controlled the votes in the party?

a.best: It let him place supporters in party positions

b.best: Stalin held more support inside the party machine

problems.detail: 'Trotsky was removed from the party and sent into exile in 1929' puts both events in 1929. Trotsky was expelled from the party in November 1927 and sent into internal exile at Alma-Ata in January 1928. Only his deportation from the USSR was in 1929. Suggested fix: 'Trotsky was expelled from the party in 1927 and deported from the Soviet Union in 1929.'
